questions: What decision will this research support, and which personal data is truly necessary?
Which seed identifiers are independently known (name, location, employer, username, image)?
What would distinguish the subject from namesakes?
Which findings require two independent sources?
steps: Record scope, authority, retention period, and prohibited data before collection.
Normalize known identifiers and record spelling, transliteration, and date variants.
Search exact names with discriminating context; prefer primary public records and first-party pages.
Pivot to public usernames, professional profiles, documents, and media without assuming identity equivalence.
Build a dated timeline and relationship candidates; label each as observed, inferred, or unknown.
Corroborate material identity links with independent attributes and preserve cited artifacts.
Minimize or redact unrelated personal data before reporting.
stop_conditions: Stop when the purpose has been answered with sufficient corroboration.
Stop before contacting the subject, triggering notifications, accessing non-public content, or collecting unnecessary sensitive data.
Escalate for legal review when minors, protected classes, medical data, precise home locations, or imminent-risk situations are involved.

questions: What legal entities, brands, jurisdictions, and date range are in scope?
Is this due diligence, public exposure review, threat intelligence, or another defined purpose?
Which sources are authoritative for registration, ownership, filings, and leadership?
steps: Resolve the official legal name, identifiers, registered jurisdiction, and first-party domains.
Collect registry filings, beneficial ownership where lawfully public, LEIs, and regulator disclosures.
Map brands, subsidiaries, directors, officers, locations, and public contact patterns.
Review public web content, archives, indexed documents, news, and official social accounts.
If explicitly authorized, inventory the organization's passive internet footprint and public breach notifications.
Corroborate ownership and control relationships; record effective dates and conflicting sources.
Produce a source-backed profile, timeline, relationship graph, gaps, and risk indicators.
stop_conditions: Do not probe logins, test credentials, interact with staff, or perform active scanning without separate written authorization.
Do not treat data-broker aggregation as authoritative without primary-source confirmation.
Stop collection that falls outside the named entities, jurisdictions, and date range.

questions: Is the domain owned by the authorized organization and explicitly in scope?
Is the task passive footprinting only, or is active testing separately authorized?
Which time period matters: current state, historical state, or both?
steps: Record the exact domain and proof of scope.
Query RDAP, DNS, certificate transparency, passive DNS, and web archives.
Inventory indexed hosts, public documents, technologies, and third-party dependencies using passive sources.
Compare present and historical records; distinguish observed infrastructure from inferred ownership.
Check public breach metadata only through authorized or verified-domain services.
Preserve source URLs, timestamps, screenshots or WARC captures, and relevant response data.
Report exposure and confidence without converting passive observations into intrusion attempts.
stop_conditions: Do not port-scan, brute-force, exploit, enumerate private endpoints, or submit URLs to public scanners when confidentiality requires a private scan.
Do not infer ownership from a shared IP, CDN, certificate, or analytics ID alone.
Stop when passive sources become repetitive and the scoped questions are answered.

questions: Is the handle public, and what independently known attributes can corroborate identity?
Could the handle be common, recycled, impersonated, or shared?
Which platforms and languages are relevant to the purpose?
steps: Search the exact handle with WhatsMyName, Sherlock, Maigret, and search engines within reasonable rate limits.
Open every candidate result and manually confirm it is a real public profile rather than a false positive.
Record stable platform IDs when lawfully visible, profile URLs, names, bios, dates, outbound links, and avatar hashes.
Compare avatars, writing, location, links, and timelines; treat each as a separate indicator.
Build candidate identity clusters and require multiple independent indicators before merging them.
Preserve relevant public pages and document negative or unavailable results as time-bound observations.
stop_conditions: Do not attempt logins, password resets, CAPTCHA bypass, blocks, or access to private profiles.
Do not report same-username matches as the same person without corroboration.
Stop automated checks when a platform disallows them or returns rate-limit/block signals.

questions: Is the address publicly listed, organization-owned, self-owned, or otherwise authorized for checking?
Is the goal discovery, verification, attribution, or exposure notification?
Would a check send a message or notification to the address owner?
steps: Derive likely organizational formats only from public examples and label unverified candidates clearly.
Use first-party contact pages, public documents, Hunter, or equivalent licensed sources for discovery.
Use non-notifying validation methods permitted by the provider and record false-positive limitations.
Use HIBP only for self-owned, authorized addresses, or verified organizational domains; retain breach metadata rather than passwords.
Corroborate attribution with public role, domain, and profile evidence.
Minimize the address in reports when the full value is not required.
stop_conditions: Do not use account-recovery flows that may alert the person or change account state.
Do not send test messages, enumerate private services, or store leaked credentials without explicit legal authority and an approved handling system.
Stop when the purpose can be met with a role address rather than a personal address.

questions: Is the available file original, recompressed, or a screenshot/download?
What exactly must be established: origin, identity, location, time, manipulation, or context?
Could the media expose a vulnerable person's location or identity?
steps: Preserve the original file unchanged, compute SHA-256, and record how it was obtained.
Extract metadata with ExifTool and technical properties with FFmpeg/ffprobe; treat metadata as claims requiring context.
For video, extract representative keyframes; run OCR and reverse-image searches across multiple engines.
Inspect signs, language, road markings, shadows, weather, architecture, terrain, reflections, and edits.
Correlate candidate locations with maps, streetside imagery, satellite imagery, SunCalc, and dated weather or event records.
Build a provenance and chronology assessment; distinguish file timestamp, upload timestamp, and depicted time.
Preserve derivatives separately and record that they were derived from the original artifact.
stop_conditions: Do not overwrite, strip, enhance, or re-encode the preserved original.
Do not publish precise locations of vulnerable people or sensitive facilities without a documented necessity review.
Do not treat a single reverse-image match or AI geolocation result as proof.

questions: What precision is necessary and proportionate: country, city, site, or exact coordinates?
What date or season is depicted?
Which observable clues can be independently verified?
steps: List observable clues before searching to reduce confirmation bias.
Use reverse-image search and OCR to generate candidates, not conclusions.
Compare roads, transit, utilities, signs, businesses, terrain, architecture, vegetation, and driving side.
Validate candidates in Google Maps/Earth, OpenStreetMap, Mapillary, satellite imagery, and historical imagery where available.
Check sun angle, weather, construction history, and event timing when the date matters.
Document matched and mismatched features and calculate the required precision.
Withhold unnecessary exact coordinates in dissemination.
stop_conditions: Do not trespass, fly drones, surveil a residence, or conduct on-site reconnaissance without separate authority and safety planning.
Do not expose a sensitive or vulnerable person's real-time location.
Stop when remaining uncertainty cannot be resolved from lawful public sources.

questions: Which platform, account, date window, keywords, and public interactions are in scope?
Is an official API available and permitted for the intended use?
Which stable account identifiers are visible?
steps: Use native search and approved APIs before third-party scrapers.
Record the profile URL, visible stable ID, display name, bio, creation date, and access time.
Collect only relevant public posts, comments, media, tags, and outbound links within the date range.
Analyze interaction patterns and timelines as indicators; do not equate engagement with a real-world relationship.
Capture relevant pages with Hunchly or ArchiveBox and hash downloaded media.
Corroborate deleted or historical material through archives and independent sources.
Review platform terms, privacy, minimization, and reporting redactions before dissemination.
stop_conditions: Do not use deceptive friend requests, impersonation, private-group access, or automated login scraping by default.
Do not bypass blocks, rate limits, CAPTCHAs, or privacy controls.
Stop collection of unrelated friends, followers, minors, or sensitive personal content.

questions: What event, geography, time window, and decision are in scope?
Which official, journalistic, eyewitness, sensor, and archival sources are available?
What misinformation or coordination hypotheses must be tested?
steps: Define the event vocabulary, languages, spellings, hashtags, geography, and UTC time window.
Collect official records and first reports, then broaden to news, social, media, archives, and public datasets.
Normalize all timestamps to UTC while preserving displayed local time and source timezone.
Verify media origin, location, and chronology; identify reposts and earliest known public appearances.
Build an event timeline and source-claim graph with contradictions and information gaps.
Assess source independence, incentives, proximity, and corroboration.
Report what is known, likely, disputed, and unknown with confidence and cut-off time.
stop_conditions: Do not amplify harmful content or publish identities/locations of vulnerable people without necessity.
Do not rely on engagement metrics or repeated reposts as independent corroboration.
Stop or escalate when collection creates physical, legal, or psychosocial risk.
